key_insight: POET-X scales the POET orthogonal-equivalence reparameterization to be memory- and compute-efficient, preserving the training stability and spectral properties of weight matrices while dramatically lowering overhead compared with the original POET implementation.
problem_solved: Reduces the high memory consumption and computational overhead of spectrum-preserving orthogonal reparameterizations when training large language models, enabling stable POET-style optimization at LLM scale.
method: Introduce a memory-efficient scaling / factorization of orthogonal equivalence transforms so orthogonal updates no longer require storing or multiplying full auxiliary matrices.
Preserve spectral properties of each weight matrix (spectrum-preserving reparameterization) to retain POET's stability while replacing expensive operations with lightweight equivalents.
Design the reparameterization to be plug-and-play with standard optimizers and model architectures, so it can be applied across layers with minimal runtime and memory impact.
impact: Makes spectrum-preserving, stability-oriented training practical for large-scale LLMs, allowing practitioners to gain POET's optimization benefits without prohibitive memory or compute costs—better scalability and reliability during training.
visual_elements: Side-by-side bar chart: memory & compute of original POET vs POET-X vs vanilla training

paper_title: POET-X: Memory-efficient LLM Training by Scaling Orthogonal Transformation
paper_authors: Zeju Qiu, Lixin Liu, Adrian Weller, Han Shi, Weiyang Liu
